title: Hotel booking requirements
idea: Scoping a hotel booking system means naming who books, what they book (a room type for a range of nights), the no-overbooking rule, and what v1 skips.
points: Guests search dates, pick a room type, pay, and may cancel later.
The core rule: never sell more rooms of a type than exist per night.
Guests book a room type; the front desk assigns a room at check-in.
Assume many searches per booking, and spikes around holidays and weekends.

edges.caption: The guest starts with dates and a guest count, and sees room types with nightly prices.
Choosing a room type holds one unit of it for every night of the stay.
A confirmed reservation can be cancelled. The CancellationPolicy decides the refund.
At arrival the front desk picks a real Room of the booked type and checks the guest in.

edges.label: later
edges.caption: The reservation only names a type. The room number is chosen on the day.

edges.label: expires
edges.caption: The system is an actor too: it frees unpaid holds and marks guests who never arrive.
Demand-based pricing, loyalty points and rate management screens wait for a later version.

code.title: Use cases and the stay rule
code.caption: The scope as code: each use case has one actor, v1 is a named range, and a stay is a half-open date range.

walk.text: v1 is the use cases from SEARCH to NO_SHOW. The rest are out.
Print each use case with its actor and an IN or OUT tag.
Four actors: guest, front desk, the system itself, and hotel admin.
Seven use cases in v1, then two that are listed but cut.
Stay a ends on the day stay b starts. Do they clash?
Check-out is exclusive, so back-to-back stays share no night.

pitfalls: Do not book a room number at search time; book a room type and assign later.
Agree that check-out is exclusive, or back-to-back stays look like overlaps.
Forgetting the system actor hides hold expiry and no-shows until late in design.

quiz.q: Why do guests reserve a room type instead of a room number?
options: Room numbers are secret from guests
Any free room of that type can serve them
Room types are cheaper to store in the database
Payment gateways cannot charge for a specific room
quiz.why: Counting units per type per night keeps rooms interchangeable. The desk can then fit stays together on the day, instead of fragmenting specific rooms.

takeaway: Book a room type per night; assign the real room at check-in.

starters: Should overbooking on purpose be in scope, like some hotels do?
Why is check-out exclusive in the date range?
